summary: Describes Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV), a control channel attached to a pseudowire along with operations such as connectivity checking. It works across the access circuit and transport types defined for pseudowires. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: A pseudowire is a pretend wire across a network. VCCV adds a side channel to send test pings, so you can tell whether the pretend wire really works.

questions: how does vccv work over l2tpv3
subtitle: A built-in side channel that lets two routers test whether a pseudowire really carries traffic end to end.

tldr.problem: Operators need a way to check the true operational state of a pseudowire from one end to the other, and to diagnose it when something is wrong.
tldr.mechanism: VCCV defines a control channel tied to the pseudowire. The two edge routers advertise which channel types and which checks (ICMP Ping or MPLS LSP Ping) they support during signaling, pick one channel type, and then send test messages that travel like the pseudowire's own data and are intercepted at the far edge.
tldr.outcome: It gives MPLS and L2TPv3 pseudowires a common fault-detection and diagnostic tool. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 5586.

today: RFC 5085 is a Proposed Standard that has not been obsoleted, but it has been updated by RFC 5586, so read the two together.

sections.title: Why Pseudowires Need a Health Check
sections.content:
A pseudowire (PW) emulates a service such as a T1 leased line or Frame Relay across a packet network. To the customer devices at either end, it looks like an unshared link. Operators told the IETF, in RFC 4377 and RFC 3916, that they need end-to-end fault detection and diagnostics to learn a pseudowire's true operational state.

Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV) is the answer. In its simplest description, it is a control channel between the pseudowire's ingress and egress points over which connectivity verification messages can be sent.

The architecture has two Provider Edge (PE) routers that terminate the pseudowire and two Customer Edge (CE) routers attached through attachment circuits (ACs), such as a Frame Relay DLCI, an ATM VPI/VCI or an Ethernet port. VCCV runs between the two PEs, as laid out in the PWE3 architecture of RFC 3985.
sections.eli5: Imagine a secret tunnel between two houses. VCCV lets the two houses send little test notes through the tunnel to check that it still works, without bothering the people living inside.

sections.title: How VCCV Works
sections.content:
VCCV has three parts: a way to signal VCCV capabilities to the peer PE, an encapsulation for control channel messages that lets the receiving PE intercept and process them locally as OAM messages, and specifications for the operational modes carried inside those messages.

When a pseudowire is first signaled with LDP (RFC 4447) or L2TPv3 (RFC 3931), the setup message carries VCCV capability information. It tells the receiving PE which combinations of Control Channel (CC) Types and Connectivity Verification (CV) Types the sender can receive. If the receiver agrees to set up the pseudowire, it returns its own capabilities in the next signaling message.

Once the pseudowire is up, the PEs may send VCCV messages. The encapsulation lets the control channel be handled like the pseudowire's data traffic, so it tests the real data plane, while the PE intercepts it instead of forwarding it out the AC toward the CE. VCCV can be run on a timed schedule for proactive checks or on demand for manual ones. The CV Types are LSP Ping (RFC 4379) for MPLS pseudowires and ICMP Ping (RFC 792, RFC 4443) for both MPLS and L2TPv3 pseudowires.
sections.eli5: First the two routers agree on how they will pass notes and what kind of note to send. After that, they can send test notes that follow the same road as normal mail, but the mailroom at the far end grabs them before they reach the customer.

sections.title: CC Types and CV Types
sections.content:
The CC Type says which kind of control channel is used. The CV Type says which protocol is carried over it. A router can support several CV Types at once but only one CC Type. Both fields are 8-bit bitmasks, so each defined type is one bit.

For MPLS pseudowires the CC Types are Type 1 (bit 0, 0x01), a PWE3 control word with 0001b as first nibble, Type 2 (0x02), the MPLS router alert label, and Type 3 (0x04), the pseudowire label with TTL equal to 1. The MPLS CV Types are ICMP Ping (0x01) and LSP Ping (0x02). For L2TPv3 there is one CC Type, an L2-Specific Sublayer with the V-bit set (0x01), and one CV Type, ICMP Ping (0x01). All other bits are reserved.

After the two sides compare what they sent and received, a PE selects only types present in both, effectively a logical AND of the bitflag fields. The chosen CC Type MUST be the only one used until the pseudowire is re-signaled. Because the interface parameters are part of the FEC, LDP rules make it impossible to change them once the pseudowire is set up, so a different set of types means re-signaling. If no type is supported, both fields SHOULD be sent as 0x00, and if no capability is signaled at all the peer MUST be treated as having no VCCV capability.
sections.eli5: Each way of passing a test note gets its own little switch, like a row of light switches. The routers compare which switches each one has, and they can only use a way that both of them have.

sections.title: VCCV over MPLS Pseudowires
sections.content:
On MPLS pseudowires, VCCV packets travel over the same LSP, either in band with the pseudowire data or out of band. They are never forwarded past the PE toward the CE. Each CC Type works differently.

Type 1 uses the PW Associated Channel Header from RFC 4385. It works only on pseudowires that use a control word in the Generic PW MPLS Control Word format, and it MUST be supported when the control word is present. The header starts with the nibble 0001, then Version and Reserved set to 0, then a Channel Type of 0x0021 for IPv4 or 0x0057 for IPv6.

Type 2 puts the MPLS router alert label immediately above the pseudowire label. It works with or without a control word and is the preferred mode when no control word is present. Type 3 sets the TTL of the pseudowire label to 1 so the destination router handles the packet in its control plane. For both, the RFC warns that ECMP hashing may differ from the data traffic, so the test could take a different path. If a control word is in use on the pseudowire, it MUST also be included before the VCCV message.

For CV Types, ICMP Ping uses an ICMP Echo packet, ICMPv4 if signaling used IPv4 addresses and ICMPv6 if it used IPv6. LSP Ping follows RFC 4379 and MUST carry a target FEC Stack with a sub-TLV that identifies the pseudowire being verified.
sections.eli5: There are three ways to slip a test note into the tunnel: mark it with a special header, put a special flag sticker on it, or make it expire at the very next stop. Each has a small catch, so the routers choose one and stick with it.

sections.title: VCCV over L2TPv3 Pseudowires
sections.content:
L2TPv3 already has a Hello keepalive, but it covers only the group of sessions on one control connection. VCCV can test an individual L2TP session, which helps troubleshoot the data plane of the endpoints and the status of single pseudowires.

A VCCV message travels in band with the session and follows the same path as user data, because the IP header and L2TPv3 session header are identical. The egress LCCE intercepts it and checks the signaling and forwarding state of the pseudowire. To carry it, the pseudowire MUST use an L2-Specific Sublayer that defines a V-bit. This document defines the V-bit as bit 0 in both the Default sublayer and the ATM-Specific sublayer. When the V-bit is 1, a VCCV message follows. The next three bits MUST be 0 when sending and are ignored on receipt, and the other 28 bits (Version, Reserved, Channel Type) follow RFC 4385.

The message MUST contain an ICMP Echo packet. In the Echo request the destination address is the remote LCCE's tunnel endpoint address, the source is the local one, and the TTL or Hop Limit is set to 1.
sections.eli5: L2TPv3 already checks whether the whole road is open. VCCV checks one single lane of that road, by sending a note whose first bit says 'this is a test, not mail'.

sections.title: Advertising and Choosing Capabilities
sections.content:
A PE that wants VCCV MUST say so during pseudowire setup. For MPLS it includes the VCCV interface parameter sub-TLV (0x0C, assigned in RFC 4446) in the setup message: in the interface parameter sub-TLV of the PW ID FEC (FEC 128), or in the Interface Parameters TLV of the Generalized PW ID FEC (FEC 129). The value is two bytes, one for CC Types and one for CV Types. For L2TPv3, the VCCV Capability AVP (Attribute Type 96) does the same job in the ICRQ, ICRP, OCRQ and OCRP messages.

The remote side MUST NOT send VCCV messages until the capability is signaled, and then only using types the peer indicated. A PE that gets VCCV messages before advertising the capability MUST discard them and not reply, and SHOULD increment an error counter. The absence of the parameter means no OAM support, and a VCCV parameter with no options set MUST be ignored. For L2TPv3, requesting CC Type 0x01 without an L2-Specific Sublayer that defines the V-bit means the session MUST be disconnected with a CDN message.

When several CC Types match, the receiver picks one by precedence: Type 1 first, then Type 2, then Type 3. For MPLS pseudowires, LSP Ping is the default CV Type and ICMP Ping is optional. Changing the CC Type after it is in use is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: Before sending test notes, each router says which kinds it can read. If there is more than one choice in common, they use a fixed pecking order, and they do not switch halfway.

sections.title: Congestion and Rate Limits
sections.content:
VCCV traffic is recommended to be minimal compared with the pseudowire it checks. Its bandwidth is taken outside any allocation for pseudowire data and can be configured, and network planning needs to count both.

CV applications MUST consider congestion and bandwidth usage. Outgoing VCCV messages SHOULD be rate-limited to avoid congestion, denial-of-service effects or an excessive packet rate at the CE-bound PE, except where rate limiting could be harmful because it might lead to wrongly declared connectivity failures. If those conditions cannot be followed, an adaptive loss-based scheme SHOULD be used so VCCV competes fairly with TCP; RFC 3448 (TFRC) is one example. ICMP and MPLS LSP Ping SHOULD be limited to below 5% of the pseudowire's bit-rate, using the full rate for constant bit-rate pseudowires such as TDM and the mean or sustained rate for variable ones such as Ethernet.

Policing of incoming VCCV messages should not be more strict than the bandwidth allocated to the VCCV channel, to avoid false indications of failure.
sections.eli5: Test notes must be small and not too frequent, like checking a pipe with a gentle tap rather than a hammer, so the checking does not clog the pipe it is checking.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC names three areas of concern. The first is control plane attacks on the signaling of VCCV capabilities. The added negotiation does not change the security aspects of Section 8.2 of RFC 4447 or Section 8.1 of RFC 3931, and source address filters may help.

The second is data plane attacks on the channel itself. An intruder could intercept or inject VCCV packets to produce false positives or negatives, or flood a peer with VCCV messages. A misconfigured device can do the same by accident. Mitigations include message throttling, which matters most where a central processor handles VCCV messages forwarded by line cards. Implementations MUST provide a way to secure the data plane, for example IPsec on MPLS packets or a private MPLS network where no external MPLS packets can be injected. For L2TPv3, the Session ID provides traffic separation and the optional Cookie adds protection, a 64-bit Cookie being usable for the most protection.

The third is the content of the messages themselves, so the security considerations of LSP Ping, ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 apply as well.
sections.eli5: A bad guy could fake test notes or flood the mailroom with them. So routers slow down how many notes they accept and keep the tunnel itself protected.
